correctness.rationale: For each t>0, A^T A has eigenvalues 1+2t² and 1, giving exact optimal squared Frobenius rank-one residual 1. Orthogonal projections onto each original row give residuals 1+t², 1+t² and 1. The first Gaussian pivot selects the last row iff (2t−1)|S|>|D| for independent S,D~N(0,2), and D/S is standard Cauchy, giving the exact two-point law. At t>1/2, complementary probability equals (2/pi) arctan(1/(2t−1)), yielding expected loss ~t/pi. The first pivot depends only on first Gaussian sketch column for all sketch widths. Exact rational identity checks and independent angular numerical integration passed; these support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: A natural first-pivot primitive in randomized interpolative decomposition can be correct with probability approaching one while suffering unbounded expected approximation-error inflation, even under perfect least-squares refitting, on a nonnegative fixed-size matrix. The exact visibility boundary t=1/2, Cauchy success probability and sketch-width invariance clarify a genuine high-probability/mean-risk gap; they do not overstate failure of a complete algorithm.
